title: Chapter 36
content:
Lurking near the galley, Jakyeong waited until a man in chef's whites stepped into the restroom. He slipped in behind him, drove an elbow into the man’s carotid until his eyes rolled back, and stripped the uniform from his limp frame. After binding the worker’s wrists and ankles and shoving him into the janitorial closet, Jakyeong pulled on the double-breasted jacket and headed toward the main kitchen.

It was peak dinner service. The kitchen was a roaring furnace of clattering pans, shouting line cooks, and rising steam—far too chaotic for anyone to notice an unfamiliar face slipping through the prep line.

Navigating past the bustling stations, Jakyeong found the dry-storage bay and scanned the shelving units until his eyes caught the small chalk mark Wang Ryun had left on a wooden crate.

He pried the lid open, revealing a thick bed of fresh, dark-green scallions. Reaching deep beneath the produce, his knuckles met the rigid contour of hard tactical polymer. He replaced the lid and hoisted the heavy crate onto his shoulder.

Just as he turned to exit, his luck ran out—a senior line cook stepped directly into his path, eyeing him with sharp displeasure.

"You the new guy?"

"Yes, sir..."

"Who gave you clearance to dig around in dry storage?"

Jakyeong’s mind raced through the roster. "Chef Kim sent me down to grab this..."

"Kim Young-woo?"

Naturally. You can never go wrong betting on a Kim in Korea.

"Yes, sir... Chef Kim Young-woo."

"What did he tell you to bring up?"

The cook closed the distance. Jakyeong tipped the wooden crate slightly, allowing him a glimpse of the scallions.

"Green onions, sir."

"Idiot. You're supposed to transfer what you need into a prep bin, not lug the whole damn crate out like a pack mule."

"My apologies, sir."

Jakyeong bowed deeply. The cook clicked his tongue in irritation and waved a dismissive hand, gesturing for him to get moving.

Exhaling a quiet breath of relief, Jakyeong slipped past the line, keeping his head down to avoid lingering gazes as he navigated toward the vessel's waste collection bay.

The door closed behind him, plunging him into the sour stench of compacted trash. Stripping off the chef's whites, he changed back into his tailored suit. He retrieved the suppressed sidearms, combat blades, and smoke canisters from the false bottom of the crate, strapping them securely into his modular harnesses beneath his jacket.

Cracking the door open, he spotted Choi Ki-tae strolling down the far end of the corridor. Jakyeong flattened himself against the recess of the wall until the man rounded the corner, then quietly took the service stairs up to the second-floor mezzanine.

As he walked down the carpeted upper hallway, a live trio—violin, cello, and grand piano—began a sweeping classical performance on the ballroom stage below. The sound drew the attention of the entire room. Draped in glittering evening gowns and bespoke tuxedos, the guests below looked for all the world like attendees at a storybook royal ball.

Jakyeong glanced down over the polished brass railing—and stopped dead in his tracks.

He narrowed his eyes, leaning forward to verify the silhouette. What the hell is he doing here...?

Standing near the edge of the ballroom floor, watching the performance with a crystal flute of champagne in hand, was Kang Il-hyun.

Just as Il-hyun began to turn his head toward the mezzanine, Jakyeong dropped flat onto his knees, tucking his entire body beneath the solid panel of the railing. Fuck...!

A floor steward noticed him crouching on the carpet and hurried over. "Sir? Are you feeling unwell?"

Jakyeong nodded quickly, keeping his face turned away.

[I am fine,] he replied in fluent Mandarin, pitching his tone into a breathless murmur. [Just a sudden spell of vertigo.]

Recognizing the language, the steward switched to Mandarin, asking if he required an escort back to his stateroom. Jakyeong shook his head, using the steward's body as a visual screen while he slowly rose to his feet with his back to the ballroom.

Glancing sideways through the glass balustrade, he confirmed Il-hyun’s attention had returned to the stage. Standing at Il-hyun's side was a stunning woman in a backless evening gown, their posture radiating an easy, familiar intimacy.

Offering the steward a quiet word of thanks, Jakyeong hugged the wall, moving with measured, silent strides until he slipped back inside his stateroom.

Wang Ryun was sprawled across the mattress, looking utterly miserable without a smartphone to pass the time. Hearing the door latch, he sat up.

"You're back? Where's the hardware?"

Jakyeong drew back his lapels, revealing the holstered sidearms.

Catching the dark, brooding storm brewing behind Jakyeong's wire-rimmed glasses, Ryun’s face grew serious. "What happened? You look like you just saw a ghost."

"He's out there."

"Who?"

"Kang Il-hyun."

Ryun stared at him, his mouth falling open. "Why the hell is he here?"

"I don't know. He told everyone he was flying to Hong Kong until tomorrow morning. Why he's on this ship..."

Ryun sprang up from the bed, pacing the narrow cabin with his hands on his hips.

Jakyeong set his jaw, drew one of the suppressed pistols from its holster, and ran a quick tactical check on the slide and magazine. Why Il-hyun was here didn't alter the mission parameters. As long as Jakyeong remained unseen, the objective stood: eliminate Choi Moon-sung within the operational window, rendezvous with Ryun’s extraction boat idling off the starboard quarter, and vanish into the night.

"Can we still pull this off?" Ryun asked.

"It doesn't change anything. He hasn't spotted me."

Jakyeong checked his watch.

Through the shared wall, the muffled sounds of rhythmic thumping and breathless moaning drifted from the adjacent suite. Ryun tucked a cigarette behind his ear and grimaced toward the plaster. "Starting early, aren't they?"

He pressed an ear against the wall, listening to the shrill, coquettish pleas filtering through the partition with an amused squint.

Before he could offer another crude commentary, a sharp knock shook their cabin door. Ryun recoiled from the wall in a flash, looking guilty as charged.

Jakyeong gestured for him to answer while turning his back toward the window to keep his face obscured.

The door opened to reveal a neatly groomed hostess. She offered a formal bow, handed over a digital tablet, and glided away down the hall.

Ryun tapped the screen, browsing the catalog. Displayed on the display were high-resolution portfolios of male and female escorts, complete with physical measurements, height, weight, and specialty services. Profiles that had already been reserved were watermarked with a red lock icon.

"If anyone catches your eye, feel free to order," Ryun said, tossing the tablet onto the bed.

Ryun had been in a devoted, long-term relationship for years and never strayed; for all his rough mercenary bravado, a single sharp word from his partner reduced him to an obedient puppy.

Jakyeong pushed the tablet aside. "Not interested."

They spent the remaining hours locked down in the cabin, having room service deliver a discreet dinner to avoid roaming the corridors. With three hours left before the operation went live, minimizing exposure was paramount.

Lying on the mattress, the image of Kang Il-hyun standing in the ballroom kept surfacing in Jakyeong's mind. Why come to this floating den? It was possible Il-hyun had financial stakes in the Choi family's distribution network, just like Seok-joo. Yet having the man lie about an overseas trip only to materialize aboard this vessel left an unsettling, bitter prickle of betrayal in Jakyeong’s chest.

He caught the thought and sat bolt upright, thoroughly disturbed by his own reaction.

When Ryun looked over with a questioning glance, Jakyeong simply shook his head, reclined back against the pillows, and forced his mind to go cold—clearing away every stray emotion until only the tactical blueprint of the kill remained.

Past midnight, the corridors thinned out as most of the revelers retreated into their private suites.

Jakyeong stepped into the hallway wearing a pair of dark, infrared-capable sunglasses. Lewd groans and ragged pants bled through nearly every doorway—the complimentary narcotics had clearly kicked the party into full swing.

Armed security details loyal to Choi Ki-tae maintained rigid patrols along the mezzanine. Looking down into the atrium, only a handful of late-night drinkers remained scattered across the lounge. Fortunately, Kang Il-hyun was nowhere in sight.

Jakyeong approached an enforcer stationed near the grand staircase, pulling a thick stack of 50,000-won banknotes from his pocket and lowering his voice to a hushed murmur.

"Excuse me... I'm looking to secure a heavier supply of gear. Price is no object. Give me the highest purity you have."

The guard sized up Jakyeong’s demeanor, then spoke into his radio.

Moments later, a well-groomed man in an executive suit and wire glasses ascended the stairs. He offered a crisp, professional bow, politely requesting to inspect Jakyeong’s invitation and keycard.

The brass name tag pinned to his lapel identified him as an Operations Director—a man Jakyeong remembered seeing glued to Chairman Choi’s side during the opening toasts.

"If you'll return to your suite and wait, I will have the package delivered to you personally," the director said with a polished smile.

Jakyeong gave a docile nod.

Just as the director turned on his heel, every light aboard the vessel died in a single, instantaneous surge.

The luxury liner was plunged into pitch-black darkness.

Murmurs of confusion instantly swelled through the corridors. The startled director reached for his radio, frantically calling for maintenance. The passengers and general staff had surrendered their mobile phones at the boarding gate, leaving them completely blind without a single pocket light to guide them.

Below, security guards scrambled with heavy emergency lanterns, but their narrow beams barely made a dent in the cavernous, multi-story atrium.

Behind the lenses of his infrared sunglasses, however, the entire corridor resolved into crisp, green-hued thermal clarity.

Jakyeong closed the distance with silent, purposeful strides, slamming his shoulder hard into the director's chest.

The impact knocked the man off balance, sending his radio clattering across the carpet as he grabbed frantically for the brass railing.

"Ah!"

"My apologies," Jakyeong gasped, pitching his voice into a frightened stammer. "I can't see a thing in the dark."

"It's quite alright, sir. Please remain in your room. We will deliver your requested items the moment the primary grid is restored."

Even in the dark, the director’s professional composure was immaculate.

Jakyeong smoothly scooped up the dropped handheld radio and coiled earpiece from the carpet, took three cautious steps backward, and slipped down the service hallway in the opposite direction.

Behind him, cabin doors cracked open as anxious guests began spilling out into the hall, while crew members rushed back and forth trying to calm the crowd.

Wang Ryun had infiltrated the sub-deck and severed both the primary generators and the secondary backups, but an auxiliary bypass would likely engage within thirty minutes. Once the engineers realized the lines had been deliberately sabotaged, the entire vessel would go on maximum lockdown.

He had less than thirty minutes to find Choi Moon-sung and put him in the ground.

Jakyeong picked up his pace, weaving effortlessly between the disoriented guests stumbling through the gloom. Crew members with flashlights were already ushering patrons back toward their quarters.

Slipping the stolen earpiece into his ear, the syndicate's internal security frequencies crackled to life with overlapping voices:

[Auxiliary lines have been physically cut.]

[Lock down all main gangways and double the perimeter watch.]

[What's the repair estimate?]

[Approximately thirty minutes to splice the main feed.]

[Get that fucking grid back online now! Put every available man on the deck and sweep for the intruder. Security team, the second the monitors flicker, pull the backup server logs and scrub every second of footage!]

It was Choi Ki-tae’s voice, barking with furious authority.

[Understood, sir.]

[And divert extra manpower to the VIP thermal suites immediately.]

[How many men, boss?]

[Are you braindead?! Send every spare gun we have down there—my father is inside right now!]

Jakyeong pulled up the architectural blueprint of the vessel in his mind.

The VIP spa and massage suites were situated at the absolute rear of the first deck. Whether the old man was receiving a legitimate treatment or indulging in illicit vice, the zone had been crawling with guards long before the blackout.

Taking the rear service stairwell, Jakyeong descended to the lower deck.

Sure enough, a dense cluster of armed enforcers was already fortifying the corridor outside the VIP suites, their faces illuminated by battery-powered work lamps and flicking lighters.

Tucking himself behind the reinforced bulkhead, Jakyeong retrieved two smoke canisters from his tactical harness.

He pulled the pins and hurled both cylinders down the hall.

The canisters struck the deck, violently hissing as thick, suffocating plumes of chemical smoke erupted in rapid succession, blinding the corridor in an opaque, gray fog.

The security detail descended into instant chaos.

"What the hell is this?!"

"Get a fire extinguisher!"

"Is that a fire? Put those damn lighters out!"

Coughing fits and frantic shouts tore through the corridor. Jakyeong yanked his tactical mask up over the bridge of his nose, held his breath, and charged straight through the smoke.

Reaching the inner foyer, the interior staff was already in a full-blown panic. Jakyeong threw his arms up, shouting in a commanding, urgent tone:

"Fire has breached the main galley! Evacuate immediately! Move! Clear the deck!"

Masseuses and attendants screamed, stampeding toward the emergency exits, throwing the remaining guards into disarray.

As Jakyeong advanced deeper into the suite, a security guard stepped forward through the haze, aiming a flashlight straight into his face.

"Identify yourself!"

Jakyeong slid his infrared glasses down the bridge of his nose, meeting the man's eyes with a smooth, disarming smile.

"Don't you recognize me?"

The guard took a step closer to inspect his features.

Jakyeong’s fist exploded forward, driving into the guard's jaw with bone-crunching force. As the man staggered back, Jakyeong launched off his back foot, driving a vicious heel straight into his sternum and dropping him to the deck.

Drawing a combat trench knife from his waistband, Jakyeong poised the blade to sever the guard's carotid—

The ship's emergency circuit tripped.

Blinding, high-intensity fluorescent light flooded the corridor.
